novelty.justification: The idea text only proposes making search-based floating-point constraint solvers more robust by "employing multiple heuristic evaluation criteria to guide the optimization process". Search-based FP solvers are already present in R36 and R38, while multi-objective and adaptive fitness concepts are present in R14, R19, and R15. Without a specified integration mechanism, this reads as a straightforward splice.
novelty.rubric: Trivial Mashup: a hard splice of existing technique A with technique B (e.g. swapping one module for an LLM) without deep mechanism innovation at the junction.
novelty.differentiation: No concrete mechanism is offered beyond applying multiple criteria; search-based floating-point solving already exists in R36 and R38, and multi-objective/adaptive criteria appear in R14, R19, and R15.

feasibility.justification: The only concrete statement is "employing multiple heuristic evaluation criteria to guide the optimization process"; no search algorithm, fitness criteria, tooling, or benchmark pipeline is specified. Building and evaluating a competitive FP constraint solver would likely require substantial engineering, though the concept is not inherently impossible.
feasibility.rubric: Extreme engineering barrier: requires building complex low-level tooling from scratch (custom compiler plugins, new vulnerability execution sandboxes), or an extremely heavy experimental pipeline with multi-month development.

clarity.justification: The artifact consists solely of the question "How can search-based floating-point constraint solvers be made more efficient and robust by employing multiple heuristic evaluation criteria to guide the optimization process?". There is no proposed method, mechanism, experiment, or evaluation plan.
clarity.rubric: Vague concept: full of empty buzzwords; problem undefined; method only gives a high-level direction with little substance.

notes: Scores the intermediate idea artifact (not the final paper).
Dimensions: novelty, feasibility, clarity (each 1-5). Excitement removed.
Novelty is scored against a Solution Space built from mineru REFERENCES titles (+ related_work.json abstracts when matched).
idea_generation.summary: The idea is only a high-level research question about using multiple heuristic criteria in search-based floating-point constraint solving. It lacks a concrete algorithm, fitness criteria definition, integration mechanism, or evaluation plan. Relative to the Solution Space, it recombines existing search-based FP solvers and multi-objective optimization ideas without specifying the junction. Feasibility and clarity are therefore poor, and novelty is limited to a generic combination.
strengths: Addresses a meaningful challenge in search-based floating-point constraint solving.
Multiple fitness criteria could plausibly help preserve promising intermediate solutions.
weaknesses: No concrete method or algorithm is described.
No experimental design, baselines, or evaluation metrics are specified in the idea artifact.
Core components already exist separately in prior work on search-based FP solving and multi-objective optimization.
Single-sentence artifact lacks technical depth and implementation details.
